reporting-org.narrative: United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East

description.narrative: UNRWA will provide legal aid to 520 refugees to support documentation, representation, and access to status-related services. Four legal clinics will operate across Jordan, guided by a needs assessment and in coordination with partners such as UNHCR and the International Committee of the Red Cross, with a focus on particularly vulnerable groups, including those residing in Garden Camp. One-time protection subsidies will assist 1,465 families with legal expenses and transportation to medical facilities. UNRWA will also provide human rights training to 120 staff and stakeholders to ensure PRS-specific protection needs are integrated across services. Rehabilitation support will reach 1,000 refugees with disabilities, including physical, occupational, speech, and autism-related therapies, as well as special education. In Garden Camp, 350 individuals will receive mental health and psychosocial support to address the effects of bullying, violence, child labour, and early marriage, building on initiatives from 2022 to 2024, in partnership with the Jordanian Institute of Family Health. To improve livelihood opportunities, 250 vulnerable refugees, including PRS, women-headed households, persons with disabilities, unemployed youth, and those registered under UNRWA’s Social Safety Net Programme, will participate in three-month vocational and life skills training in repair and maintenance, designed to enhance self-reliance through a circular economy approach. Community-based organizations will involve 5,000 refugees in awareness sessions addressing gender-based violence, risk reduction, and harmful social norms.
